title: I cheated with the die. The picture didn't care.
desc:
Lab clip · Issue 02, Experiment 3

Loading a die in the chaos game changes how fast each part of the Sierpinski triangle fills in, but it does not change the shape: the holes stay exactly where they were.

THE RULE
Three corners. One dot. Roll a die, jump halfway towards the corner it picks, mark the spot, repeat. Do that enough times and the Sierpinski triangle appears.

THE CHEAT
Now load the die so corner 1 comes up nine times out of ten. The picture goes lopsided, crowded at the top and starved at the bottom. But after three quarters of a million dots, not one of them has landed in a hole, and every hole is in the same place as before.

WHY
A crooked die changes how often each region gets visited. It cannot change which points are reachable, because every roll is still a jump into one of the three half-size corner triangles, and the middle one is never a corner triangle. The die picks the route; the rule picks the shape.

TRY IT YOURSELF
The board in this clip is the real one, free to open:
https://interactiveexplorer.space/math-universe
Drag "Load the die towards corner 1" up to 90%, press Run, and watch where the dots refuse to go.

FOR THE CLASSROOM (10 minutes, paper and one die)
Mark three corners on a sheet and start anywhere. Faces 1-2 mean corner A, 3-4 corner B, 5-6 corner C. Jump halfway, mark the spot, repeat forty times. Then load the die: corner A also takes a 5, so A now wins half the throws. Forty more marks. Pool the class's sheets on one wall - the crowding changes, the gaps do not.

Four more experiments and one open problem are in Issue 02 of The Math Universe Lab. Guess what a different jump, a sixth corner and a rule with no die at all each do, then watch the issue and see.
